Combine WithinHostExperiment objects by rows or columns

Source: R/methods.R
WHE-combine.Rd

Methods for the combineRows and combineCols generics. combineRows combines objects vertically (adding variant sites); all objects must have the same samples (columns). Samples are matched by their column names: an object that holds them in another order is put in the first object's order, and one that holds other samples is an error naming them. The colData and the metadata are the first object's. combineCols combines objects horizontally (adding samples); all objects must have the same variant sites (rows). Sites are matched by sequence name, position, ref and alt: an object that holds them in another order is put in the first object's order, and one that holds other sites is an error counting them. Objects read from separate files usually hold different sites; read the files together with readWithinHost instead, which takes the union. QC logs and filters from all objects are merged.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment'
combineRows(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment'
combineCols(x, ..., use.names = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A WithinHostExperiment.

...

Further WithinHostExperiment objects to combine.

use.names

Accepted for compatibility with the generic. Sites are matched by sequence name, position and alleles, not by row name.

Value

A WithinHostExperiment.

Examples

data(example_whe)
whe1 <- example_whe[1:10, ]
whe2 <- example_whe[11:nrow(example_whe), ]
merged <- combineRows(whe1, whe2)
nrow(merged) == nrow(example_whe)
#> [1] TRUE

whe_d <- example_whe[, 1]
whe_r <- example_whe[, 2]
merged <- combineCols(whe_d, whe_r)
ncol(merged)
#> [1] 2
